h1: Weekend Timing Tips: Why an Early Visit Beats the Rush
meta_description: Planning a weekend visit to Bakudan Ramen? Here's how hours and timing work across all three San Antonio locations.
supporting_keywords: best time to go to Bakudan Ramen
image_alt: A table spread of ramen and side dishes at Bakudan Ramen
body_html:
Weekend hours at Bakudan run a little longer than weekdays, and that extra time gives you more room to plan around when it's actually busiest.

Friday and Saturday Hours

All three locations are open 11:00 AM–9:00 PM on Friday and Saturday, an hour later than the 8:30 PM weekday close. Sunday hours run 11:00 AM–8:00 PM, matching Monday through Thursday.

Earlier Tends to Be Easier

An 11:00 AM opening means an early lunch is a realistic option on a weekend, and generally an earlier visit — whether that's lunch or an early dinner — is a more relaxed time to go than the middle of a Friday or Saturday evening, when weekend dinner traffic tends to peak at most restaurants.

Ordering Ahead Helps Regardless of Timing

If you can't avoid a busier window, ordering ahead through Toast for pickup is a way to skip an in-person wait even during a location's busiest stretch.

Happy Hour Still Applies on Weekends

The daily 3–6 PM happy hour runs every day, including weekends, so an early-evening visit before the dinner rush can also line up with happy hour pricing depending on the location.

No Guarantees, Just Better Odds

None of this guarantees a specific wait time — that depends on the night and the location. But earlier timing and ordering ahead are the two most practical levers you actually have control over.
